passageText: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
plainMeaning: The phrase introduces the start of creation and places God before the created order.
symbolicMeaning: Beginning functions as origin, foundation, and the first point in a meaningful ordered reality.
literaryContext: Opening phrase of Genesis and the Bible itself.
historicalContext: Part of the Hebrew Bible creation account, received in Jewish and Christian traditions.

interpretations.label: Origin Reading
interpretations.summary: The phrase frames creation as purposeful beginning rather than random appearance.

passageText: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
plainMeaning: God commands light to exist, and light appears.
symbolicMeaning: Light can represent order, revelation, life, visibility, and the first separation from darkness.
historicalContext: Part of the creation sequence in Genesis.

passageText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
plainMeaning: John introduces the Word as existing from the beginning.
symbolicMeaning: The Word connects speech, meaning, reason, divine self-expression, and creation.
literaryContext: Opening concept of the Gospel of John.
historicalContext: John 1 uses Logos language that became central in Christian theology.
